cells.tense: You're here, feeling it open before you know what it's for.
cells.verb: letting feeling surface before there's anything yet to feel about
cells.place: where you can see the whole shape of a thing and still stand inside it
cells.ask: Offer it one next place to deepen — let what you've seen stay open to becoming truer than it is today; what comes back is a knowing that keeps going deeper the longer you stay with it.
cells.core:
You're here before the feeling has a name. Something in you has opened and nothing has been poured in yet — and you're letting that be enough instead of reaching for the first thing to fill it. The same eyes that take in the whole shape of a thing are wide right now, and you're not rushing them shut.
A knowing like that doesn't close the book. It just turns the page.
cells.sheetLine: You're open before you know what for, and you're letting it stay open.

cells.tense: You're already feeling how it will go, ahead of anything actually happening.
cells.verb: opening ahead of the moment instead of in it
cells.place: where you watch the whole shape of things from just outside them
cells.ask: Offer your next move instead of forcing it — pick one thing you're pushing and choose the direction with your eyes open rather than your grip tight; what comes back is choosing from clarity rather than from the need to be sure.
cells.core:
You're feeling everything ahead of time. Before anything has actually happened, you've already taken the shape of what might — the disappointment, the next need, the way it could go — so your heart is wide open to a future nobody has handed you. From where you're watching, every shape is visible at once, and none of them is here yet.
The opening is real. It's just aimed past the moment it belongs to.
cells.sheetLine: You're feeling it before it happens, and the bracing has become the feeling.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that closed behind you.
cells.verb: keeping the heart shut where it once opened
cells.place: where the whole shape was visible and you're looking from far enough out that it's hard to enter
cells.ask: Offer your attention to one thing in front of you that isn't settled yet — let it be brand new to you, even something you think you know; what comes back is being actually here, open and ready, each moment fresh again.
cells.core:
The opening happened and you weren't in the room for it. Somewhere back there, feeling something made things harder, and putting your own eyes outside the situation got you through — and it still does. You can see the whole shape of things from here. You just can't feel your way back inside it.
The capacity didn't go anywhere. It went quiet.
cells.sheetLine: You see the whole shape from here. You just can't feel your way in.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you're already writing in.
cells.verb: already open and calling it something else
cells.place: where you see the whole shape and treat it as ordinary
cells.ask: Offer the plainest true thing you can see — the one you already know without working for it — and say it as the knowing it is, not as a mood or a guess; what comes back is perception that lands on its own, no argument needed.
cells.core:
You're already wide open to what's in front of you — people feel it, it shapes how you listen — and you'd tell me you're just being aware, just paying attention, nothing special. Meanwhile the reading of the whole room keeps happening anyway, quietly, under whatever you call it.
The seeing is running. It just isn't being counted by the one it belongs to.
cells.sheetLine: You're already open to it. You just haven't called it your knowing.
